title: Job assignment by logic-based Benders decomposition
description: Assign jobs to machines so that the assignment cost plus the total tardiness is smallest, with logic-based Benders decomposition: the master problem (an optimal abstraction) assigns jobs and estimates the tardiness of each machine, the subproblem (an optimal check) sequences each machine. A too-low estimate gives an optimality cut, grounded as rules from refine(k); it holds for every assignment that gives the machine a superset of the jobs. track draws the lower bound (the optimum of the master) and the upper bound (the best feasible cost) until they meet. One solution: an optimal assignment. Optima checked against one clingo program that assigns and sequences at once.

fragments.name: shared
fragments.text:
% The instance (Instances tab): job(J,P,D) has processing time P and due date D;
% cost(J,M,C) is the cost of running job J on machine M.
machine(M) :- cost(_,M,_).
total(S) :- S = #sum { P,J : job(J,P,_) }.
njobs(N) :- N = #count { J : job(J,_,_) }.
% No machine can have more total tardiness than this.
top(T) :- total(S), njobs(N), T = S * N.

fragments.name: abstraction
fragments.text:
% The master problem: which machine runs each job, and an estimate est(M,V) of the total
% tardiness on machine M. The estimate starts free (0 is cheapest); optimality cuts from the
% subproblem raise it.
1 { assign(J,M) : machine(M) } 1 :- job(J,_,_).
1 { est(M,V) : V = 0..T } 1 :- machine(M), top(T).
% The tags assign and est keep the two sums apart: without them, a cost and an estimate
% with the same (value, number) tuple would be counted once.
#minimize { C,J,assign : assign(J,M), cost(J,M,C) }.
#minimize { V,M,est : est(M,V) }.
#show assign/2.
#show est/2.

#program refine(k).
% A Benders optimality cut from the k-th subproblem. cut(k,has(M,J)): machine M ran job J;
% lateness(k,late(J,L)): job J was L late. If machine M gets at least these jobs again, its
% tardiness is at least their total lateness V: more jobs never make the tardiness smaller.
need(k,M,V) :- machine(M), cut(k,has(M,_)), V = #sum { L,J : lateness(k,late(J,L)), cut(k,has(M,J)) }.
covered(k,M) :- need(k,M,_), assign(J,M) : cut(k,has(M,J)).
:- covered(k,M), need(k,M,V), est(M,E), E < V.

fragments.name: glue
fragments.text:
glue(assign(J,M)) :- job(J,_,_), machine(M).
glue(est(M,V)) :- machine(M), top(T), V = 0..T.

fragments.name: check
fragments.text:
% The subproblem: sequence the jobs on each machine to minimise the total tardiness
% (solved with 'optimal'). before(A,B): A runs before B on their machine.
same(A,B) :- assign(A,M), assign(B,M), A < B.
{ before(A,B) } :- same(A,B).
before(B,A) :- same(A,B), not before(A,B).
:- before(A,B), before(B,C), before(C,A).
wait(J,S) :- assign(J,_), S = #sum { Q,I : before(I,J), job(I,Q,_) }.
done(J,F) :- wait(J,S), job(J,P,_), F = S + P.
late(J,L) :- done(J,F), job(J,_,D), L = F - D, L > 0.
#minimize { L,J,late : late(J,L) }.
% A machine whose estimate is below its real tardiness (a comparison, not a computed sum:
% the sums stay out of the grounding) gets a cut, built from its jobs and their lateness.
bad(M) :- est(M,E), #sum { L,J : late(J,L), assign(J,M) } > E.
has(M,J) :- bad(M), assign(J,M).
#show bad/1.
#show has/2.
#show late/2.

loop.text:
solver A = shared + abstraction
solver C = shared + check
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

# Logic-based Benders decomposition (Hooker and Ottosson): the master assigns jobs and
# estimates each machine's tardiness; the subproblem sequences the jobs and computes the real
# tardiness. Where an estimate is too low, an optimality cut (rules, grounded from refine(k))
# raises it for every assignment that gives that machine at least these jobs. The master's
# optimum is a lower bound; the master's cost corrected by the real tardiness is a feasible
# cost, an upper bound. They meet at the optimum.
upper = none
loop:
    M = A.solve(optimal)
    if not M: stop "no assignment"
    X = C.solve(assume G(M), optimal)
    # a feasible cost: the master's cost with the estimates replaced by the real tardiness
    claimed = 0
    for e in M.atoms(est/2):
        claimed = claimed + e.arg(2)
    cost = M.cost - claimed + X.cost
    if upper == none or cost < upper: upper = cost
    track lower = M.cost
    track upper = upper
    if X.count(bad/1) == 0:
        log "optimum:", M.cost
        accept M
        stop
    count cuts by X.count(bad/1)
    A.expand(refine, cut = X.atoms(has/2), lateness = X.atoms(late/2))

library.summary: Logic-based Benders decomposition: a master assigns jobs to machines and estimates their tardiness; the subproblem sequences them and returns optimality cuts as rules; lower and upper bounds tracked (6 jobs, 2 machines, optimum 20, 1 solution).
